subject: Marketplace baseline basket minimum + channel credit routing
messages:
From: Jake Morris <jake.morris@healthlytics.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@healthlytics.com
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify basket minimum and channel credit routing for Azure private offer

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Healthlytics is working through the Azure private offer and we need to align on two things before we proceed:

1) Basket minimum handling across multiple SKUs: our commercial team wants a single "baseline basket" that ensures list-price anchoring across the mix (node-hours + reserved capacity + support). If some SKUs undershoot the minimum, how do you prefer to reconcile — per-SKU true-up vs. pooled basket true-up?

2) Channel crediting / margin: we work with a regional reseller (BrightBridge) and a distributor. Healthlytics needs to understand how credits/discounts flow to partner invoices so our finance team can book net-of-channel. Specifically: how do marketplace discounts translate to reseller margin and distributor fees on the invoice path? Can you provide an example invoice or waterfall?

We also need the procurement-friendly evidence (sample invoice path, a one-page summary we can attach to our PO, and any required reseller onboarding docs).

Attached is our draft PO template (we will send the signed PDF later). Can we get a written note of the recommended flow and a short call early next week?

Thanks,
Jake Morris
Head of Procurement
Healthlytics
(Attachment: healthlytics_po_template.pdf 72KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jake Morris <jake.morris@healthlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify basket minimum and channel credit routing for Azure private offer

Hi Jake — thanks for the clear note and the PO template. High level answers below, plus I attached a small worksheet that lays out the invoice waterfall and two reconciliation options.

Short answers:
- Basket approach: we recommend a pooled-basket true-up (single baseline basket). It smooths commit volatility and minimizes per-SKU admin. We can support per-SKU true-ups if your accounting requires SKU-level accounting, but there is extra reconciliation overhead.
- Channel crediting: typical flow is (1) Azure private-offer discount applied at listing level -> (2) Redwood passes a channel credit to reseller via partner settlement (Gross-to-Net routing) -> (3) Distributor fee is paid out of partner settlement or invoiced separately depending on your reseller arrangement. In practice we map the discount into a waterfall that preserves the reseller margin target and surfaces a distributor fee line for audit.

Example (from the attached workbook):
- List price: $1,000,000 baseline basket
- Private offer discount: 20% -> customer pays $800,000
- Reseller margin target: 12% of list -> $120,000
- Distributor fee: 5% of list -> $50,000
- Net to Redwood (pre-tax): $800,000 - $120,000 - $50,000 = $630,000

If you prefer, we can present the same math as net-of-commission so your finance team sees the booked revenue directly. The worksheet (marketplace_basket_flow_v1.xlsx) has both views and a sample invoice layout that shows the lines your AP team will see.

Next steps I propose:
- I will share the attached workbook now.
- If pooled-basket is acceptable, confirm and we will build the private offer with commit buckets and a quarterly true-up.
- If you need reseller-specific accounting (BrightBridge split), send the reseller legal name and billing entity so we can show the exact settlement path.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call Tues or Wed morning PST to walk through the worksheet.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: marketplace_basket_flow_v1.xlsx 24KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>

- Ask Legal to pre-clear our sample invoice language (I can chase Legal once we have Healthlytics' reseller billing entity).
- Prepare an alternate workbook tab showing a per-SKU true-up (for their controller). That avoids back-and-forth later.

I'll be on the call if they pick the Tuesday slot.

Ben
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
